speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have some skin concerns; to begin our evaluation, can you describe the specific lesions you are worried about, including their size, shape, color, and how long they have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; your heavy smoking history and the location of these non-healing, crusty lesions are concerning. Given the previous failed treatments for syphilis and eczema, and the specific sites involved (penile shaft and finger), is there any history of trauma to these areas or a family history of skin cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions on the penile shaft and a chronic sun-exposed site (finger) in a heavy smoker with failed treatments for syphilis and eczema is highly suggestive of SCC. I recommend immediate biopsy for confirmation and staging.
